hardware_facts.statement: The +3V3 pin on the JANALOG header outputs the 3.3 V system rail (3.1 V min, 3.3 V typical, 3.5 V max).
hardware_facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, sections 3.2 'Recommended Operating Conditions' and 9.7

hardware_facts.statement: The JANALOG header carries +3V3, +5V (5V_SYS, 4.5-5.5 V from USB-C) and two GND pins.
hardware_facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, sections 3.1 'Input Power' and 9.7

hardware_facts.statement: The MCU-controlled RGB LEDs (LED3 on PH10-PH12, LED4 on PH13-PH15) are active-low: they turn on when driven to logic 0.

hardware_facts.source: arduino:zephyr 1.1.0 boards.txt, checked with arduino-cli 1.2.0 on 2026-11-14

hardware_facts.statement: Text output from a sketch reaches the computer through the Monitor object of the official Arduino_RouterBridge library (Monitor.begin(), Monitor.println()). It is routed through the board's Linux side.

Sketches are uploaded with the core's 'remoteocd' tool through the board's Linux side, not through a serial bootloader as on the classic UNO.

The matrix is driven with the Arduino_LED_Matrix library that ships with the core: declare `Arduino_LED_Matrix matrix;`, call `matrix.begin();` and `matrix.setGrayscaleBits(3);` in setup(), then `matrix.draw(frame);` where frame is a `uint8_t[104]`, row by row (8 rows of 13), each value 0 (off) to 7 (brightest).
The module has four pins: analog signal (AO), ground (G), supply (+) and digital signal (DO). The order differs between makers, so go by the printed labels.

hardware_facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi and micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.

An LM393 comparator drives DO high when the sound level exceeds the threshold set with the trim potentiometer. Powered from 3.3 V, neither output can rise above 3.3 V. The level on your module is not confirmed, so the sketch reacts to a change, not to a fixed level.

hardware_facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi and micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.

An LM393 comparator drives DO high when the sound level exceeds the threshold set with the trim potentiometer. Powered from 3.3 V, neither output can rise above 3.3 V. The level on your module is not confirmed, so the sketch reacts to a change, not to a fixed level.

wiring_steps.display_text: Unplug USB. KY-037 G to board GND
wiring_steps.spoken_text: Unplug the board's USB cable first. Then: Connect the sensor's pin labelled G to GND on the board.

wiring_steps.display_text: KY-037 + to board +3V3
wiring_steps.spoken_text: Connect the sensor's pin labelled + to +3V3 on the board.

wiring_steps.display_text: KY-037 DO to board D2. Plug USB in
wiring_steps.spoken_text: Connect the sensor's pin labelled DO to D2 on the board. Then plug the USB cable back in and check that the sensor's power LED lights up.
